source_facts: Identified four canonical BANC MDNs with super_class 'descending' and primary cell_type 'MDN'.
Direct connectivity topology and partner lists exacted from BANC v888 simple edge list.
literature_supported_facts: MDNs are necessary and sufficient command-type neurons for backward locomotion.
Asymmetric left/right MDN activity can contribute to backward turning.
MDN control is distributed through downstream motor circuits.
LBL40 and LUL130 have experimentally characterized roles in the neural pathways.
engineering_assumptions: MDN activity is abstracted as a normalized command state in [0.0, 1.0].
All four canonical MDNs are activated simultaneously with full magnitude in this demonstration.
The transition uses a discrete switch threshold/state abstraction rather than continuous integration.
MDN population command maps deterministically to an engineered adhesion phase shift of 0.55 cycles.
This mapping demonstrates a feasible mechanism but makes no claim to represent biological kinematics.
